title: Outlook for Mac: Purview DLP wait-on-send support
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, documented control paths and PowerShell examples match the sources checked. It distinguishes existing controls for other Outlook clients from the Mac settings, default and licensing that Microsoft has not yet documented.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans Purview DLP wait-on-send support for Outlook for Mac.
claims.quote: Outlook for Mac will support Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention (DLP) wait-on-send policies.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; What's changing; Why it matters; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The default state and arrival behaviour of Mac wait on send are not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook Mac DLP wait on send DLPWaitOnSendEnabled timeout licensing default. Read the roadmap, mobile/macOS policy-tip reference, new Outlook reference and Set-OrganizationConfig; defaults found concern Windows, not Mac.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn has not yet described the Mac wait-on-send feature specifically.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook Mac DLP wait on send; Outlook macOS wait send DLP roles settings. Opened mobile/macOS, classic and new Outlook policy-tip references and Mac preferences; no Mac wait-on-send feature documentation found.

claims.where: summary; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: The Mac wait-on-send switch and timeout configuration are not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook macOS wait send DLP roles settings. Opened Set preferences for Outlook for Mac, Set-OrganizationConfig and the mobile/macOS policy-tip reference; no Mac wait-on-send setting was documented.

claims.claim: Outlook for Microsoft 365 wait on send is configured using the dlpwaitonsendtimeout registry key.
claims.quote: After you've configured the Oversharing dialog, you can optionally enable the **Wait on send** dialog feature using the *dlpwaitonsendtimeout Registry key (DWORD value)*.

claims.claim: The Group Policy setting for classic Outlook is named Specify wait time to evaluate sensitive content.
claims.quote: You can set this *RegKey* via group policy, **Specify wait time to evaluate sensitive content**, script, or other mechanism for configuring registry keys.

claims.claim: DLPWaitOnSendEnabled and DLPWaitOnSendTimeout control wait to send in new Outlook for Windows.
claims.quote:
The wait‑to‑send experience is controlled solely through the following Exchange mailbox parameters:

- **DLPWaitOnSendEnabled**

claims.claim: The mobile/macOS reference's wait-on-send section says Android and iOS, not macOS, do not yet support it.
claims.quote: Outlook for Android and iOS doesn't yet support *DLP Wait‑to‑Send, which is* centrally managed

claims.claim: For Outlook for Microsoft 365, an unconfigured or disabled wait-on-send setting sends the message immediately.
claims.quote: **Not configured** or **Disabled**: This is the default. When *dlpwaitonsendtimeout* isn't configured, the message isn't checked before the user sends it. The email message is sent immediately once **Send** is clicked.

claims.claim: In that classic Outlook case, the DLP service evaluates the message and applies policy actions after immediate sending.
claims.quote: The email message is sent immediately once **Send** is clicked. The DLP data classification service evaluates the message and apply the actions defined in the DLP policy.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated whether Mac behaves like classic Outlook when wait on send is not enabled.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook Mac DLP wait on send DLPWaitOnSendEnabled timeout licensing default; Outlook macOS wait send DLP roles settings. Read mobile/macOS policy tips, Mac preferences and Set-OrganizationConfig; no corresponding Mac behaviour stated.

claims.claim: For Outlook for Microsoft 365, waits of 0 to 9999 seconds offer Send anyway if evaluation has not completed within the configured wait.
claims.quote: If the policy evaluation doesn't complete in the specified time a **Send anyway** button appears allowing the user to bypass the presend check. The **T** value range is 0 to 9999 seconds.

claims.claim: For Outlook for Microsoft 365, a timeout above 9999 is replaced with 10000.
claims.quote: If the **T** value is greater than 9999, it's replaced with 10000

claims.claim: That above-9999 classic Outlook configuration holds the message until evaluation completes without a Send Anyway override.
claims.quote: the **Send Anyway** button doesn't appear. This holds the message until the policy evaluation completes and doesn't provide the user with an *override* option.

claims.claim: For new Outlook for Windows, a timeout of zero immediately shows Send Anyway.
claims.quote: When DLPWaitOnSendTimeout = 0, user will immediately see “Send Anyway” in the infobar of mail.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: Whether Mac offers the same timeout bypass is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook Mac DLP wait on send DLPWaitOnSendEnabled timeout licensing default; Outlook macOS wait send DLP roles settings. Read mobile/macOS policy tips, Mac preferences and Set-OrganizationConfig; no Mac timeout override documented.

claims.claim: Learn says a matching DLP block rule blocks the message regardless of the Policy tips configuration.
claims.quote: If the block rules defined in the DLP policy are met, the message will be blocked regardless of how **Policy tips** is configured.

claims.claim: For Outlook for Microsoft 365, evaluation duration can vary with internet speed, content length and the number of policies.
claims.quote: The duration for completing the evaluation can vary depending on factors such as internet speed, content length, and the number of policies defined.

claims.claim: Policy-tip UI is off by default in Outlook for Android, iOS and macOS.
claims.quote: Policy Tip UI is turned off by default in Outlook for Android, iOS, and macOS to allow for administrators to test and perform user training prior to deployment.

claims.claim: The licence requirement for Mac wait on send has not yet been published.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: The oversharing pop-ups getting-started page states a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription requirement.
claims.quote: Oversharing pop-ups require a Microsoft 365 **E5 subscription**, along with a version of Outlook that supports oversharing pop-ups.

claims.claim: The Outlook for Microsoft 365 reference lists its wait-on-send dialog as applying to Online E5 users with connected experience enabled.
claims.quote:
#### Applies to:

- Online E5 users with connected experience enabled
- Production version 2303 (Build 16.0.16216.10000) or higher.
- Semi-Annual Enterprise Channel version 2302 (Build 16.0.16130.20478) or higher.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; front matter: licensing.notes
claims.claim: The service description lists Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5, Purview Suite/EDU/GOV/FLW, Defender + Purview Suite FLW and Microsoft 365 E5/A5/F5/G5 Information Protection & Governance for advanced Outlook policy tips including the oversharing dialog.
claims.quote:
these licenses are required for each scoped user:

- Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5
- Microsoft Purview Suite/EDU/GOV/FLW and Microsoft Defender + Purview Suite FLW
- Microsoft 365 E5/A5/F5/G5 Information Protection & Governance

claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a price specific to Mac wait on send.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook Mac wait on send configuration role license price meter default DLP; Outlook Mac wait on send licensing price meter. Opened Purview service description and Outlook policy-tip references; no Mac wait-on-send price found.

claims.claim: No meter is documented for Mac wait on send as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook Mac wait on send licensing price meter. Read Purview service description, including Exchange DLP and advanced Outlook policy-tip licensing; no meter for Mac wait on send found.

claims.claim: Learn lists Compliance administrator, Compliance data administrator, Information Protection, Information Protection Admin and Security administrator as role groups for creating and deploying these DLP policies.
claims.quote:
The account you use to create and deploy policies must be a member of one of the following role groups

- Compliance administrator
- Compliance data administrator
- Information Protection
- Information Protection Admin
- Security administrator

claims.claim: Roles for configuring the Mac wait-on-send setting are not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook macOS wait send DLP roles settings; Outlook Mac wait on send configuration role license price meter default DLP. Opened Mac preferences, mobile/macOS policy tips and Set-OrganizationConfig; no Mac wait-on-send role requirement found.

claims.claim: The documented Outlook pre-send DLP configuration uses a policy scoped to the Exchange location.
claims.quote: To enable these pop-ups, first scope your policy to the Exchange location and then select the **Show policy tip as a dialog for the user before send** option

claims.claim: Learn names the rule option Show the policy tip as a dialog for the end user before send (available for Exchange workload only).
claims.quote: Select **Policy tips** > **Show the policy tip as a dialog for the end user before send (available for Exchange workload only)**.

claims.claim: No admin-centre path is documented for the Exchange wait-to-send parameters.
claims.quote: Searched: "DLPWaitOnSendEnabled" "admin center". Opened Set-OrganizationConfig and new Outlook policy-tip reference; the experience is described as controlled solely through Exchange parameters, with no admin UI path.

claims.claim: Set-OrganizationConfig -DLPWaitOnSendEnabled $true -DLPWaitOnSendTimeout <seconds> uses documented Exchange Online parameters for enabling wait-on-send evaluation and specifying its timeout.
claims.quote:
$true: Mail sent from Outlook for Windows to Exchange is evaluated by DLP.

To set the timeout value, use the DLPWaitOnSendTimeout parameter.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not confirmed that the Exchange parameters, classic registry key or Group Policy setting govern Mac wait on send.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook Mac DLP wait on send DLPWaitOnSendEnabled timeout licensing default; Outlook macOS wait send DLP roles settings. Read Set-OrganizationConfig, Mac preferences and all cited Outlook policy-tip pages; no Mac applicability statement found.

claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 Apps admin center path for the policy-tip setting is Customization > Policy Management.
claims.quote: You can access this policy under **Customization** and **Policy Management**.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The policy-tip policy can be targeted to individuals or groups.
claims.quote: You can target policies to individuals or groups, so you can test and deploy policy tip UI as needed through your organization.

claims.claim: The named policy governs policy-tip visibility for Android, iOS and macOS, rather than documenting a wait-on-send setting.
claims.quote: To enable Policy Tip UI to appear in Outlook for Android, iOS, and macOS, you must enable the policy listed in the following section in the Microsoft 365 Apps Admin Center.

claims.claim: No API or PowerShell equivalent is documented for the named policy-tip visibility policy.
claims.quote: Searched: "Enable Purview Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policy tips in Outlook" Graph PowerShell API cloud policy; "Cloud Policy" "API" "Microsoft 365 Apps". Read mobile/macOS policy tips and Cloud Policy search excerpts; no equivalent call found.

claims.claim: The documented Purview portal entry path for the DLP policy is Data loss prevention > Policies.
claims.quote: Sign in to the [Microsoft Purview portal](https://purview.microsoft.com) > **Data loss prevention** > **Policies**

claims.claim: The abbreviated New-DlpComplianceRule call retains the documented warn-rule parameters, including NotifyUser Owner, NotifyPolicyTipDisplayOption Dialog, the label condition and trusted-domain exception.
claims.quote: New-DlpComplianceRule -Name <DLP Rule Name> -Policy <DLP Policy Name> -NotifyUser Owner -NotifyPolicyTipDisplayOption "Dialog" -ContentContainsSensitiveInformation

claims.claim: Mac support for the documented pre-send oversharing dialog rule option has not been confirmed.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook macOS wait send DLP roles settings. Read oversharing getting-started and mobile/macOS policy-tip references; the latter's oversharing-dialog section names Android and iOS, not macOS.

claims.claim: The full New-DlpComplianceRule example reproduces Learn's warn-rule example, including its complete sensitivity-label hashtable and recipient-domain exception.
claims.quote: -ContentContainsSensitiveInformation @(@{operator = "And"; groups = @(@{operator="Or";name="Default";labels=@(@{name=<Label GUID>;type="Sensitivity"})})}) -ExceptIfRecipientDomainIs @("contoso.com","microsoft.com")

claims.where: Governance controls: Full warn-rule example introduction
claims.claim: The Label GUID placeholder identifies the sensitivity label in the example's condition.
claims.quote: Configures one or more sensitivity label conditions. This sample includes one. At least one label is mandatory.

claims.where: Governance controls: Full warn-rule example introduction
claims.claim: The example's ExceptIfRecipientDomainIs values represent trusted recipient domains.
claims.quote: | [-ExceptIfRecipientDomainIs](/en-us/powershell/module/exchange/new-dlpcompliancerule?view=exchange-ps#-exceptifrecipientdomainis&preserve-view=true) | List of trusted domains. |
